turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally got me to come in is that work is just... I can’t keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore. And honestly, those code forms are getting ridiculous lately. They updated the National Electrical Code again, and I swear the guys writing it just want to sell more heavy books. It’s a total racket, you know? 

But yeah, I try to sit down and do the paperwork, and then I hear a drill or some tool noise, or my phone buzzes with a text. Like my buddy Dave texted me about this old Chevy he's restoring—I helped him wire the alternator a couple years back. Good guy, terrible taste in beer though. Anyway, what was I saying? Right, a text, or I’ll just get some brand new idea about the workshop and how to set it up better, and it just pulls me completely off track. Next thing I know, my jobs are starting to get all mixed up.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as hearing a drill, tool noise, or his phone buzzing.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, going off-topic about code books, his friend's car, and beer preferences before losing his train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable for several days and you felt unlike your usual self?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I guess so. I’ll get into these stretches where I’m in this massive, pumped-up mood, just talking non-stop about how our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town. Which, by the way, solar is booming right now. The tax rebates are driving people crazy for it. I was down at the supply house last week talking to Jimmy—he’s this older guy who runs the counter, always wears these bright red suspenders, funny guy—and he was saying they can't even keep the inverters in stock. It's a whole supply chain mess with the overseas shipping right now. 

But anyway, I get super hyped about expanding the business, and then if my wife or one of the apprentices even slightly questions the plan, I just flip out. I get incredibly sharp with them over absolutely nothing. I mean, my wife is just trying to be practical, she's got this whole color-coded planner system she uses for our budget. I actually bought her these fancy Japanese pens for it last year for our anniversary because she loves stationary stuff... wait, what did you ask me? Right, irritable. Yeah, I get pretty snappy when I'm feeling that hyped up.

turns.doctor_question: During those pumped-up stretches, do you need less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, exactly. It’s been going on for months now, actually. I’ll go to bed, sleep maybe three, four hours max, and then boom—I’m wide awake before the sun's even up. And I don't feel tired at all. I feel completely ready to go, like I just slept for ten hours. I'll get right to pricing materials or sketching out a new solar array for a roof. 

Speaking of roofs, you wouldn't believe the pitch on this one house we looked at last week. It was like a ski slope. The homeowner, this guy named Arthur, he’s a retired dentist or something, he was out there in his bathrobe watching us measure it. He had this little terrier dog that kept barking at my boots. I don't know what it is with small dogs and work boots, but they always go nuts. My sister has a pug, and that thing... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, I just pop right up, ready to answer emails and get the day started on barely any sleep at all.

turns.doctor_question: During those pumped-up times, do you feel more powerful or capable than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, absolutely. I keep getting this intense feeling that I can just instantly take on massive commercial jobs and, like, train an entire crew of guys right this second. Like, you know that new high-rise they're putting up over on 4th street? They've had cranes out there for six months. My buddy Mike works on the structural steel side of things, and he was telling me about how they had to completely reroute the plumbing because the blueprints got botched by the architect. 

Architects, man, I swear they draw these pretty pictures but never think about how we're actually supposed to run the conduit through a solid concrete beam. I remember this one guy in my intro to drafting class back at community college, he always used to wear these ridiculous fedoras and insist on using charcoal instead of pencils. Made a huge mess of his desk every single day. Super weird guy. I wonder whatever happened to him. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling capable. Yeah, so I get this feeling I can run a whole commercial operation, even though, if I really stop and think about it, part of me knows my current licensing and my actual experience aren't quite where they need to be to legally pull that off yet. But when I'm in that zone, I just feel totally bulletproof.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and derailment, wandering from commercial jobs to a specific construction site, to architects, and to a former classmate before losing their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient confirms feeling 'totally bulletproof' and believing they can instantly take on massive commercial jobs and train a crew, despite acknowledging they lack the necessary licensing and experience.

turns.doctor_question: During those pumped-up periods, have you done things that got you into serious trouble, like major spending, dangerous decisions, or problems at work or home?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it's definitely causing some friction. Like, at work, clients have started complaining about missed details and mixed-up scheduling. I had this one lady, Mrs. Higgins, she was furious because I told her we'd be there Tuesday to wire up her new hot tub, but I completely forgot I’d booked us across town. Hot tubs are a nightmare anyway, you gotta run a dedicated 50-amp circuit, usually trenching through the yard. And you wouldn't believe the roots we hit at the last place. Oak trees, man. They just spiderweb everywhere. My neighbor has this massive oak that drops acorns all over my driveway, sounds like hail when they hit the truck roof. I keep meaning to ask him to trim it back, but he's this retired guy who just sits on his porch all day polishing his golf clubs. 

Anyway, where was I? Oh, right, the scheduling stuff. Yeah, so the clients are getting mad, and my apprentices, they just don't trust my direction the way they used to. They're second-guessing me. And then at home... man, it's rough. The mortgage and the business are turning into constant arguments. My wife feels like I’m putting everything we built at risk. She gets so stressed she starts baking. We had like three dozen blueberry muffins on the counter last weekend. Which is great, I love muffins, but... yeah, it's just a lot of fighting right now.

Well, this whole thing has been building for about seven months now. It really started right around the time we took on the mortgage for the new workshop and all the upgraded equipment. My loan officer, this guy named Kevin, he kept losing my emails. I'd send him the P&L statements, and three days later he'd call asking for the exact same documents. He had this really annoying habit of chewing ice while we were on the phone. Just crunch, crunch, crunch right in my ear. 

It made me think about my old dentist, Dr. Berman, he always told me chewing ice is the worst thing you can do for your enamel. Anyway, yeah, it's been about seven months since we got the mortgage and all this really started ramping up.

turns.doctor_question: Before these past seven months, did you have the same kind of trouble focusing and getting distracted when you were a kid?
turns.patient_response:
No, I don't think so. I was pretty locked in as a kid. Like, if I was building something, I'd just sit there for hours and not even hear my mom calling me for dinner. I used to take apart old radios and stuff out in the garage. My grandpa gave me this old ham radio when I was like ten, and I spent an entire summer just messing with the circuit boards. 

Ham radios are wild, honestly, the frequencies you can pick up if you know what you're doing. My grandpa used to talk to people in, like, Russia and Brazil on that thing. He had this massive antenna strapped to the side of his chimney. The HOA tried to make him take it down because it was an "eyesore," but he fought them tooth and nail. He actually went to the city council over it and brought all these obscure FCC regulations printed out in a binder. He was a really stubborn guy. He used to drive this beat-up old Ford Ranger that didn't even have power steering, and he refused to sell it. Said the new trucks had too many computers in them. Which, as an electrician, I kind of get, because the more sensors you have, the more points of failure you're dealing with... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, focusing when I was younger. Yeah, no, I didn't have any problems with getting distracted back then. It's really just been this recent stuff.
